page.eyebrow: Epic #734 · Wave 2 · the last of the twelve days
page.title: Day 3 against Neave's manual
page.standfirst_html:
Every text flag the comparator raised for Day 3, adjudicated against F.Day.3.13Jan20.pdf — the extracted text for wording, eight page images, the PDF's own font data, and an anchor-by-anchor check of all 46 {#sec-pageN} ids against the page each one names. Day 3 is the biggest day in the course and it has the biggest flag list: 121 flagged sentences, 47 missing paragraphs, the lowest clean rate of the twelve at 61%.

The artefact Day 3 asks you to print and cut out is a coloured bar. funnel-track-colourful.png is 2000×100 pixels and 602 bytes — red, white and blue stripes, no numbers, no squares, no funnel, no marble — and it has been the whole of printed page 59 since the file was created. What makes it more than a bad crop is that a deviation entry was written specifically to keep it, on the grounds that “the visual quotation matters because it is the artefact the reader handles”. That reasoning is right and the file does not contain the artefact; the decision was taken without opening it. The correct artwork has been sitting extracted and unused in the repo the whole time.

Three more things no automated check could see. Day 3's Approvals, Acknowledgments and Information page is missing outright — the same defect, on another day, that Day 9's pass found and that #796 was raised to chase — taking with it the rights acknowledgments for Scherkenbach's Ford histograms and every SPC Press quotation the site reproduces. A 24-value data set is transposed in all three places it appears, so the run chart and the histogram a learner draws are of numbers Neave did not print. And 18 of the 46 page anchors name a page they do not sit on, including two called sec-page5, which is what a “Day 3 page 5” link resolves against.

Emphasis is deliberately absent from this page. Day 3 has 223 emphasis runs — the corpus's largest — and they get their own record, per #825; see X-01.

items.flag: Altered 33 · 79% — scored below the near-certain band, and a real defect
items.source_html: “Deming was careful to pay due respect to ‘subject-matter experts’. <mark class='src'>In contrast,</mark> I've known teachers of Statistics who seem keen on ignoring subject-matter knowledge lest it ‘bias’ the conclusions available from the data.”
items.site_html: “Deming was careful to pay due respect to ‘subject-matter experts’: <mark class='gone'>in context,</mark> I've known teachers of Statistics who seem keen on ignoring subject-matter knowledge…”
items.evidence_html: “In contrast” became “in context”, which reverses the relation between the two sentences. Neave is setting Deming's respect for subject-matter experts against statisticians who ignore them; the site's version reads as though the statisticians are an illustration of Deming's respect. The joined sentence also loses the full stop. Two paragraphs later the source completes the pair — “At the other extreme there are some ‘subject-matter experts’ who…” — which only parses if this sentence was a contrast. This sat in the 70–89% band, the band #734 exists because #721 was not working.
items.proposal: Deming was careful to pay due respect to "subject-matter experts". In contrast, I've known teachers of Statistics who seem keen on ignoring subject-matter knowledge lest it "bias" the conclusions available from the data.

sections.title: Out of scope for a per-day pass
sections.note_html: Recorded so they are not re-discovered from scratch, and so a future reader can tell “checked, handed on” from “never looked at”.

items.flag: Never flagged — pdftotext discards every italic and bold
items.source_html: Aligning the PDF's own font data against the pandoc AST (the #825 method) finds 182 lost emphasis runs, 37 added and 4 swapped on Day 3 after site-convention filters.
items.site_html: The largest emphasis load in the corpus by a wide margin — Day 9's hand pass found 29, Day 2's 25, Day 12's 18.
items.evidence_html: Deliberately not in this pass. Adding it would have made a ~320-finding review page, four times the largest so far. #825's recommendation was to route the ~480-run corpus backlog through this same review-page flow “one day at a time, with Day 3 first”, so Day 3's emphasis gets its own record and PR and doubles as the pilot for that route. The two are independent: emphasis edits touch no file in SCORER_VERSION_FILES, so neither restales the other. #825's two open conventions — bold-vs-italic swaps and colour-only emphasis — stay with the production-checker issue rather than being settled off one day's evidence.

items.chip: Day 3's data-driven pages are frozen against their own CSVs
items.source_html: Already raised as #808.
items.site_html: Open, Day 3-specific.
items.evidence_html: Adjacent to fidelity and deliberately left alone. Nothing in this pass's flag list turns out to be a transcription defect in those pages — N-11 is the one that came closest and it cleared. Keeping the two apart avoids a pass whose diff mixes prose corrections with regenerated chart data.

items.chip: Page-range and serial-comma style beyond Day 3
items.source_html: Corpus-wide there are 186 “pages X–Y” against 16 “pages X to Y”, and eleven of the sixteen are on Day 3.
items.site_html: Fixing Day 3 leaves five outliers on appendix/03-day-3.qmd, optional-extras/05-part-e-normality.qmd, Day 4, Day 7 and Day 8.
items.evidence_html: Out of scope for a per-day pass, but worth recording so it is not re-discovered from scratch. The five are a small enough set to fold into those records' own passes — Days 4, 7 and 8 are closed, so this would be a standalone tidy or an item for the appendix passes still to come.

items.source_html: #796 is open and asks exactly this: whether every day's “Approvals, Acknowledgments and Information” page is present.
items.site_html: Day 3's is missing; Days 5, 7, 9 and 11 have one; the other seven are unchecked.
items.evidence_html: D3-05 restores Day 3's, which is in scope here. Whether the remaining seven days even have such a page in their sources is #796's question, and now has a second confirmed instance behind it — two of the five days checked so far were missing theirs.
